beats.say: A thousand balls. Fourteen landed on one edge. Not a single ball landed on the other.

head: EVERY PEG IS
TILTED 70 / 30.
beats.say: The catch: every peg is tilted. Seventy percent of bounces go right. Thirty percent go left. Twelve rows of pegs.

head: A FAIR BOARD
PEAKS IN THE MIDDLE.
beats.say: On a fair board, the middle bin should catch about two hundred and twenty six balls. This one caught eighty six.

head: THE PEAK
MOVED RIGHT.
beats.say: The whole pile moved right. The tallest bin is 8 right bounces out of 12. The math says the average is seventy percent of twelve: 8.4.
beats.speak: The whole pile moved right. The tallest bin is eight right bounces out of twelve. The math says the average is seventy percent of twelve. Eight point four.

head: RIGHT EDGE:
1 IN 72.
beats.say: Twelve right bounces in a row is a one in seventy two shot. So about fourteen balls should get there. Fourteen did.

head: LEFT EDGE:
1 IN 1,881,676.
beats.say: Twelve left bounces in a row? One in 1,881,676. With a thousand balls, zero made it.
beats.speak: Twelve left bounces in a row? One in nearly two million. With a thousand balls, zero made it.

head: SAME CURVE.
JUST SHIFTED.
beats.say: Draw the math on top. The same kind of curve, just shifted. A small tilt at every peg moved the whole crowd. Francis Galton invented this board.
Follow Ship With Pip for more.

title: Tilt every peg 70/30: 14 balls hit one edge, 0 hit the other
caption: A Galton board with a twist: every peg is tilted, so a ball bounces right 70% of the time and left 30%. 1000 balls, 12 rows. A fair board expects about 226 balls in the middle bin; this one caught 86. The tallest bin is 8 right bounces out of 12, next to the average the math predicts (70% of 12 = 8.4). Reaching the right edge takes 12 right bounces in a row, a 1 in 72 shot, so about 14 balls should get there: 14 did. The left edge is 1 in 1,881,676, and 0 of 1000 made it. The curve drawn on top is the binomial distribution for 12 bounces at 70%. Every bounce here is simulated with a seeded weighted coin flip, sped up.
notes: Seed 4477, 12 rows, 1000 balls, p(right) = 0.7. Bin counts by number of right bounces: [0, 0, 0, 2, 10, 31, 86, 148, 245, 231, 154, 79, 14]. Fair board expected middle = 1000 * C(12,6) / 4096 = 225.6, about 226. Mean rights 12 * 0.7 = 8.4; most likely bin = 9 rights (24.0%), with 8 rights close behind (23.1%); observed tallest = 8 rights (245), 9 rights 231. Script only claims the tallest observed bin and the 8.4 average. Right edge odds 1 / 0.7^12 = 72.25, about 1 in 72; expected 1000 * 0.7^12 = 13.8, about 14; observed 14. Left edge odds 1 / 0.3^12 = 1,881,676; observed 0. Sources: Wikipedia Galton board and UCL Galton collection (Galton's quincunx) for Galton inventing the board. Sync: all balls released by sim 24 s, last lands 25.6 s at the middle of beat 2; video is sped up, not real time.
